title: Migration 61 — rule enforcement status parity
description: Applies migrations 39, 40, 41 then 61, runs 61's VERIFY A-E, then rolls 61 back on a disposable PostgreSQL cluster. Two places answered 'is this rule enforced?' and disagreed about one status: the application (isRuleEnforcedNow) said approved OR active, the database (compliance_rules_currently_enforced, migration 41) said active only. Since #157 the application's answer is the one that actually stops a buyer pack, so a rule at status 'approved' could block output while the database reported it as not enforced -- a gate whose reason could not be verified from the data. The owner decided on 2026-08-07 that approved means switched on, which resolves it in the application's favour, so the DATABASE widens here. Narrowing the application instead was rejected: it would silently stop a rule that blocks a pack today from blocking it tomorrow, and quietly weakening a safety gate is not a way to tidy a mismatch. Both resolvers change, because compliance_rules_in_force already admits paused and retired precisely because those were switched on at some point -- under the same reasoning 'approved' belongs there too, and widening only one would move the divergence rather than close it.

verify.note: B is the point: an approved rule inside its window is reported as currently enforced, matching what already blocks buyer packs. Every other section exists to stop B passing for the wrong reason. C proves the widening was by ONE status and not five -- a paused rule must still not block a shipment today. D is the section a lazy implementation fails: both its fixture rows are status 'approved', one starting in 30 days and one that ended 30 days ago, so anything that widened the status filter and dropped the effective-window predicate passes A, B and C and dies here. E proves the historical resolver widened in step, and still answers the point-in-time question -- the expired approved rule IS in force at a date inside its own window, which is what makes judging a past shipment by its own date possible.
